content.value_statement: Teams need reliable guidance for Azure document extraction in TypeScript. This skill provides focused examples for OCR, layout analysis, prebuilt models, custom models, and classifiers.
actual_capabilities: Shows how to create the REST client with DefaultAzureCredential or an API key.
Explains URL and local file analysis for prebuilt document models.
Lists common prebuilt model IDs for invoices, receipts, tax forms, contracts, and bank statements.
Demonstrates custom model and classifier build workflows using Azure Blob training data.
Covers polling, pagination, error checks, and important TypeScript SDK helper types.
limitations: It is documentation only and does not run Azure requests by itself.
Users must provide their own Azure resource, credentials, files, and permissions.
Examples still require local testing against the current Azure SDK version.
It does not validate extracted data quality for regulated workflows.

use_cases.title: Extract Invoice Fields
use_cases.description: Finance teams can map vendor, total, and due date fields from invoices into review workflows.

use_cases.title: Prototype OCR Pipelines
use_cases.description: Developers can compare read, layout, and specialized prebuilt models before building a production service.

use_cases.title: Prepare Custom Training
use_cases.description: Data teams can structure Azure Blob training sources for custom models and document classifiers.

prompt_templates.title: Analyze a PDF from a URL
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to show a TypeScript example for analyzing a PDF URL with prebuilt-layout.

prompt_templates.title: Extract invoice fields
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a TypeScript flow that reads invoice vendor, total, and due date fields with Azure Document Intelligence.

prompt_templates.title: Build a custom model
prompt_templates.prompt: Guide me through a TypeScript custom model build using Azure Blob training data and long-running polling.

prompt_templates.title: Design a classifier pipeline
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a TypeScript workflow that builds a classifier, routes invoices and receipts, and validates confidence scores.

output_examples.input: Request: Analyze a sample invoice URL.
output: Returned fields include vendor name, invoice total, and due date.
Follow up by checking field confidence before saving results.

output_examples.input: Request: Build a classifier for invoices and receipts.
output_examples.output: The skill outlines Azure Blob training folders, classifier creation, polling, and result review steps.
The skill recommends the document model list endpoint with pagination and error handling.

best_practices: Check isUnexpected responses before reading result bodies.
Store endpoints, API keys, and SAS URLs outside source control.
Set confidence thresholds before sending extracted fields to downstream systems.
anti_patterns: Do not hardcode real Azure keys or SAS URLs in prompts or source files.
Do not assume every document matches one prebuilt model.
Do not skip polling for long-running analysis and build operations.

faq.question: Does this skill call Azure directly?
faq.answer: No. It provides TypeScript guidance and examples. The user runs code in their own environment.

faq.question: Which SDK does it cover?
faq.answer: It covers the Azure REST client package for Document Intelligence and related Azure identity setup.

faq.question: Can it analyze local files?
faq.answer: Yes. It shows how to read a local file, encode it, and send it for analysis.

faq.question: Does it support custom models?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes examples for custom model builds and document classifier builds.

faq.question: What credentials are required?
faq.answer: Use an Azure endpoint with DefaultAzureCredential, an API key, or a SAS URL for training data.

faq.question: Is it suitable for regulated documents?
faq.answer: It can support regulated workflows, but users must add privacy controls, validation, and compliance review.
